newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr closes higher on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr closes higher on bargain-hunting.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Monday, reflecting bargain-hunting for the local currency that emerged after initial gains by the greenback, dealers said.

Early-week commercial demand for the U.S. dollar had driven the local unit to an intra-day low of T$27.937 in early trade, but the Taiwan dollar rebounded to finish at T$27.918 against Saturday's T$27.924 close.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$287 million.
Dealers said sentiment for the Taiwan dollar was boosted by expectations that the central bank would not let the currency fall precipitously or rashly.
"Recent actions and remarks by the central bank have sapped the U.S. dollar of the bulk of its appreciation strength," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong last week gave his most explicit comment to date on the speculative pressures that have undermined several southeast Asian currencies in July -- saying Taiwan's dollar was not vulnerable.
Dealers said they had noticed heavy intervention by the central bank in recent weeks when the Taiwan dollar encountered what they described as heavily speculative selling by overseas interests.
A T$27.90-93 range was seen for Tuesday.
